public_body: Great Barrington Housing Authority Board Of Commissioners
overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving minutes late, and member Eileen Mooney violated it by emailing a quorum, intentionally; the post-adjournment call was not deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to approve meeting minutes in a timely manner, citing February 18 and March 26 minutes approved only on May 5.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve its February 18 and March 26 meeting minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Board member Eileen Mooney deliberated outside a noticed meeting through repeated emails copying the whole Board on Board business.
allegations.key_passage: When Ms. Mooney expressed her opinion on these matters to a quorum of the Board through email, she engaged in deliberation outside of an open meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Board member Mooney kept deliberating on a phone line after the March 26 meeting was adjourned.
allegations.key_passage: As Chair Mercer and Ms. Mooney merely discussed the administrative matter of distributing the meeting minutes, without expressing any opinions on the substance of those minutes, we find no deliberation and no violation of the Open Meeting Law related to the March 26 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the violations were intentional; the AG considered whether Mooney's email deliberation was a knowing violation.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find Ms. Mooney’s individual violation to be intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future determination may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
